approved_scope.title: Add specsync doctor to report every change problem with its fix and close merged changes late where older SpecSync never reads
approved_scope.description: Add specsync doctor to report every change problem with its fix and close merged changes late where older SpecSync never reads
acceptance_criteria: D5: late-closing a member of an acknowledged sequence collision drops that acknowledgement from .specsync/change-sequence.json and records it in late-close.json. The ledger sequence is never lowered, and doctor says the ledger edit needs an open change that declares it wherever meaningful files require one.
Failing tests first: each new test fails on the branch base before the implementation and passes after; no existing gate, bound, timeout or assertion is loosened.

RECOVER-3, RECOVER-3.a (REQ-cmd-change-035): `specsync doctor` reads the repository and lists every finding with its kind, its change, the reason and its fix, classed safe, decision or report-only. The kinds are: a change merged but never archived (an active package committed on the remote default branch); an accepted change whose inputs drifted, including any package in .specsync/archive/changes/ that still says accepted; a finalize that stopped halfway (accepted with finalization.json, or a v1 change accepted but not archived); stale verification; and records that another version of SpecSync wrote (5.0.1-era ledgers missing digest fields, v1 plans missing the 6.2 sections, a schema newer than the binary, a closed-late slug minted again).
RECOVER-3.b: plain `doctor` writes nothing, and `doctor --fix --dry-run` reports exactly what `--fix` would do with the same arguments and writes nothing.

RECOVER-3.c: `--fix` applies only the safe fixes: the `migrate 5.0` backfill, and resuming a stopped finalize (v1: `change archive`) when nothing blocks it. Stale verification is report-only and names `change check <id> --commit`. A late close is a decision: it applies only to changes named with `--close-late <id>...` or `--close-late all`, and only with a non-empty `--actor` and `--reason`.
RECOVER-3.d: a check that cannot run, such as a bounded Git read that overflows (#976), becomes a finding that says so, and doctor still reports every other finding.

REQ-cli-args-025: the `doctor` subcommand parses `--fix`, `--dry-run`, a repeatable `--close-late <id|all>`, `--actor`, `--reason` and the global output flags, and argument parsing refuses `--close-late` given without `--fix`, `--actor` and `--reason`.

SHIP-12, SHIP-12.c, SHIP-12.e (REQ-change-143): a late close moves the package byte for byte from .specsync/changes/ or .specsync/archive/changes/ to .specsync/archive/closed-late/<date>-<id>/, keeps its state.json and the state in it, adds late-close.json, and adds no ChangeState variant. It reads none of the change's delivery evidence, and it closes only a package committed on the remote default branch; any other is refused and nothing is written.

SHIP-12.a, SHIP-12.d: late-close.json records the actor, reason, timestamp, the state it was closed from, the workflow version, the path it came from, the remote default ref and commit, the commit that merged it and that commit's date, and verified false. `change status` (text and JSON) and `ship-status` say it was closed late, never re-checked and not verified, and a closed draft also says it was never approved.
SHIP-12.b: a closed-late change is never part of the archive preflight or the successor walk; reopen, review, check, accept, archive and finalize refuse it; and `change new` refuses its slug.
SHIP-12.f: several late closes in one call are all checked before anything is written; one refusal writes nothing and names the change refused.

SHIP-12.g, D4: a CI job and a fledge lane run real 6.0.0 and 6.2.0 Linux release binaries, pinned by sha256, against a repository after `doctor --fix`. There, audit passes; list omits the closed-late changes; status, ship-status and reopen report them not found; a partial finalize they blocked resumes and archives; a v1 archive passes; and a collision fixture audits clean.

answers.constraints: Leif's decisions via orc t18 ('Capture + recommended design', 2026-11-06), which supersede close-late as its own command and the new-state pick. Build it as `specsync doctor`, shipping in 6.3.0. The late close is one doctor fix, stored where 6.x never reads (.specsync/archive/closed-late/), with no ChangeState variant (6.0 to 6.2 refuse unknown values). It was proven against real 6.0.0 to 6.2.0 binaries, and a CI test keeps it proven. D2: stale verification is report-only. D3: --close-late <id>... or all, with --actor/--reason. D4: the compat test runs in CI. D5: a collision member drops and records its acknowledgement. Site and Corvidinho CI pin 6.0.0. Strictness stays: no gate, bound, timeout or existing assertion is loosened. No tag, release or crates.io publish.

send_backs.reason: Narrow affected_paths from all of src/ to the files this change touches, and add the cli spec (src/main.rs dispatch arm) with a Purpose delta; ship refused on src/agents.rs ownership. Code and tests unchanged.

applied_items.content:
A late close SHALL move a change package that is committed on the remote default branch but was never archived, byte for byte, into `.specsync/archive/closed-late/<date>-<id>/` with a `late-close.json` record, without reading the change's delivery evidence and without adding a change state, and SpecSync SHALL never treat a closed-late change as verified.

Acceptance Criteria
- The package comes from `.specsync/changes/` or `.specsync/archive/changes/`. Its `state.json` keeps its bytes and the state in it, and every other file keeps its bytes.
- The package's `state.json`, at its current path, must be present on the remote default reference (`origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main` or `origin/master`). When no remote default resolves, or the package is not on it, the close is refused and nothing is written.
- No delivery input, acceptance manifest, acceptance input digest or verification is read or rebuilt.
- `late-close.json` records the schema version, change ID, actor, reason, timestamp, the state it was closed from, its workflow version, the path it came from, the remote default reference and its commit, the commit that added the package and that commit's date, and `verified: false`.
- For a member of an acknowledged sequence collision, the acknowledgement is removed from `.specsync/change-sequence.json` and recorded in `late-close.json`; the ledger's sequence and claim are unchanged.
- A closed-late change is never part of the archive preflight, the successor walk or the sequence accounting, which read only `.specsync/changes/` and `.specsync/archive/changes/`.
- `change status` (text and JSON) and `change ship-status` report a closed-late change as closed late, with who, when and why, the commit that merged it and that commit's date, never re-checked and not verified; one closed from draft is also reported as never approved.
- `reopen`, `review`, `check`, `accept`, `archive` and `finalize` refuse a closed-late change, and `change new` refuses its slug.
- SpecSync 6.0.0 and 6.2.0, run against a repository holding closed-late packages, pass `change audit`, omit them from `change list`, report them not found in `change status`, `change ship-status` and `change reopen`, and are not blocked by them in `change finalize` or `change archive`.

`specsync doctor` SHALL report every problem it finds in the repository's change records, each with its fix classed as safe, decision or report-only; with `--fix` it SHALL apply only the safe fixes, and it SHALL apply a late close (REQ-change-143) only to the changes named with `--close-late`, and only with a human actor and a reason.

Acceptance Criteria
- Findings cover: a change merged but never archived; an accepted change whose inputs drifted, including an `accepted` package under `.specsync/archive/changes/`; a finalize that stopped halfway, including a workflow-v1 change accepted but not archived; stale verification; and records another SpecSync version wrote (missing 5.0.1-era digest fields, workflow-v1 plans without the 6.2 sections, a newer schema, an ID that a closed-late package already holds).
- Each finding names its kind, change, reason, fix class and the exact command or doctor flag that applies the fix. Text and JSON carry the same findings.
- A check that cannot run becomes a finding that names its error, and every other finding is still reported.
- Plain `doctor` writes nothing. `--fix --dry-run` reports exactly what `--fix` would do with the same arguments and writes nothing.
- The safe fixes are the `migrate 5.0` backfill, and resuming a stopped finalize (workflow v1: `change archive`) when no other finding blocks it. Stale verification is report-only and names `change check <id> --commit`.
- `--close-late <id>` (repeatable) or `--close-late all` closes the named or every eligible change late, only with a non-empty `--actor` and `--reason`. Every named change is checked before anything is written, and one refusal writes nothing and names the refused change.
- A late close of a collision member says that the ledger edit needs an open change declaring `.specsync/change-sequence.json` wherever meaningful files require one.

The `doctor` subcommand SHALL accept `--fix`, `--dry-run`, a repeatable `--close-late <id|all>`, `--actor <name>` and `--reason <text>`, together with the global output flags; argument parsing SHALL refuse `--close-late` given without `--fix`, `--actor` and `--reason`, and `--dry-run` given without `--fix`.

Acceptance Criteria
- `specsync doctor`, `specsync doctor --fix`, `specsync doctor --fix --dry-run` and `specsync doctor --fix --close-late a --close-late b --actor X --reason Y` parse.
- `specsync doctor --close-late a --actor X --reason Y` (no `--fix`), `specsync doctor --fix --close-late a` (no actor or reason) and `specsync doctor --dry-run` are refused by argument parsing.
